about: A Zork-like underground empire, final test. You arrive at an endless stair with your old lantern, explore passages to a sword in a rock and a sunlit cliff, where an unseen, amused person watches from above while you are stuck on a ledge with a locked chest.

done.why: I sampled about a dozen turns of the opening, enjoyed the prose, and chose to stop before reaching any goal.

moments.note: Lantern description reads like an old friend following you reluctantly.
Cliff oasis: sunlight, giant trees, something not a tree keeping still.
Could not examine the thing among the trees even though the text pointed to it.
Descending the rope brings an unseen watcher who reacts to my actions.
Calling up gets a wry, patient answer hinting that the chest should be sent up.

wished: Examine the watcher among the trees
Find a way to send the chest up or get the key

lines.line: From somewhere above you, at the top of the cliff, somebody finds this funny, briefly, and stops.
lines.why: A refusal message that also characterizes an unseen presence.

lines.line: Somebody is at the top of this rope, and is in no hurry to say so.
It has the look of an old friend who has followed you somewhere it would rather not have come.

fun.why: Short but charming, with reactive details.

engagement.why: The watcher hook made me want to continue.

difficulty.why: Too little played to judge; the rope puzzle looks fair but unclear.

interestingness.why: The sequel feel and the watching figure are intriguing.

prose.why: Descriptions are precise, witty and atmospheric, and the world's reactions are well written.
